chapters.title: PLAYING PILGRIMS
chapters.notes: Read all 94 paragraphs. Sisters remain present; Father is only a letter writer. Separate nine-o’clock music from sewing and Hannah’s table-clearing.

scenes.title: Christmas Without Presents

states.jo: Jo lies by the parlor fire and protests that Christmas cannot be Christmas without presents.
states.meg: Meg looks at her worn dress and laments the family’s poverty.
states.amy: Amy complains that other girls possess the pretty things she lacks.
states.beth: Beth reminds her sisters that they still have one another.

scenes.reason: Opening conversation establishes the four sisters, the room, and their separate burdens.

scenes.title: Four Gifts for Marmee

states.jo: Jo warms Marmee’s worn slippers and claims the duty of replacing them while Father is away.
states.meg: Meg abandons her own purchase and chooses gloves for Marmee.
states.amy: Amy chooses cologne while hoping to preserve part of her dollar.
states.beth: Beth proposes that all four spend their dollars on Marmee instead of themselves.

scenes.reason: The clock and sight of Marmee’s slippers turn complaint into a concrete Christmas plan.

scenes.title: The Christmas Rehearsal

states.jo: Jo directs the melodrama, demonstrates Amy’s faint, and performs the villain with gusto.
states.meg: Meg rehearses the leading role and laughs through the production’s mishaps.
states.amy: Amy attempts the fainting scene with more stiffness than anguish.
states.beth: Beth watches admiringly until the toast burns.

scenes.reason: The sisters move from gift planning into embodied rehearsal with changed actions and props.

scenes.title: Marmee Comes Home

states.marmee: Marmee returns from preparing wartime aid boxes and settles among her daughters.
states.jo: Jo helps make the room comfortable and guesses that the promised treat is a letter.
states.meg: Meg arranges the tea table and speaks proudly of Father’s voluntary service.
states.amy: Amy sits on Marmee’s lap and imagines the discomforts of camp life.
states.beth: Beth waits quietly and asks when Father can come home.

scenes.reason: Marmee enters, changing the present cast and focus from playacting to family news.

scenes.title: Father’s Letter

states.marmee: Marmee reads Father’s letter beside the fire and lets its appeal reach each daughter.
states.jo: Jo hides behind the chair, weeps openly, and resolves to do her duty at home.
states.meg: Meg hears Father’s hopes and resolves to complain less about work and appearance.
states.amy: Amy sobs against Marmee and admits her selfishness.
states.beth: Beth wipes her tears with the army sock and begins knitting with renewed purpose.

scenes.reason: The family gathers around the letter; each sister’s state changes in response.

scenes.title: Pilgrims in Earnest

states.marmee: Marmee turns the childhood Pilgrim’s Progress game into a guide for daily self-conquest.
states.jo: Jo embraces the romance of making duty a pilgrimage and asks for directions.
states.meg: Meg recognizes the game as a practical way to keep trying to be good.
states.amy: Amy asks literal questions about burdens and agrees to begin again.
states.beth: Beth names housework, envy, and fear of strangers as her burden.

scenes.reason: Marmee introduces the governing pilgrimage metaphor and each sister accepts a goal.

scenes.title: Sewing the Four Continents

states.jo: Jo divides the long seams into four imagined continents to make the sewing pass pleasantly.
states.meg: Meg sews the sheets without complaining after accepting the new pilgrimage.
states.amy: Amy works through the long seams while talking about the countries.
states.beth: Beth joins the ungrudging sewing after naming her daily burden.
states.marmee: Marmee stays with her daughters as their new resolutions become household work.
states.hannah: Hannah clears the supper table while the family discusses its new plan.

scenes.reason: The family moves from counsel into shared work and the nightly musical custom; Hannah becomes directly present.

scenes.title: The Evening Choir

states.meg: Meg leads the family’s customary songs with her clear voice.
states.marmee: Marmee sings with Meg at the close of the working evening.
states.beth: Beth accompanies the family softly on the old piano.
states.amy: Amy adds her chirping voice to the familiar choir.
states.jo: Jo wanders through the tune and repeatedly arrives at the wrong note.

scenes.reason: At nine the sewing stops and the household begins its distinct musical custom; Hannah is no longer directly shown.

chapters.title: A MERRY CHRISTMAS
chapters.notes: Read all 74 paragraphs. Correct the bedroom theatre, Amy’s role, and Hannah’s entrance; supper follows downstairs. Christmas guidebooks appear here, not during Father’s earlier letter.

scenes.title: Books Under the Pillows

states.jo: Jo wakes disappointed, finds the crimson guidebook, and reads cheek to cheek with Meg.
states.meg: Meg begins the Christmas reading and quietly draws Jo into it.
states.amy: Amy values her blue-covered book and joins Beth in reading.
states.beth: Beth offers to help Amy with difficult words and reads beside her.

scenes.reason: Christmas morning begins upstairs with the sisters and their books.

scenes.title: The Hidden Basket

states.jo: Jo dances in the new slippers and teases Beth about the handkerchief initials.
states.meg: Meg checks the hidden gifts and reassures Beth that the marking will please Mother.
states.beth: Beth displays her carefully marked handkerchiefs and worries about her choice of initials.
states.hannah: Hannah reports Mother’s charitable errand and gets breakfast ready.

scenes.reason: The sisters go downstairs; Hannah joins the cast and Amy returns from an offstage errand.

scenes.title: Amy’s Larger Bottle

states.amy: Amy returns hooded and cloaked with the larger cologne bottle bought using all her money.
states.meg: Meg questions Amy, then hugs her for the unselfish exchange.
states.jo: Jo calls Amy a trump after learning that she spent her whole dollar.
states.beth: Beth chooses her finest rose to decorate Amy’s stately bottle.
states.hannah: Hannah remains at the household breakfast preparations as Amy brings back her gift.

scenes.reason: Amy enters after an offstage purchase; her arrival and sacrifice change the present cast and the gift’s ownership.

scenes.title: Marmee’s Christmas Request

states.marmee: Marmee returns and asks her hungry daughters to give their breakfast to the Hummels.
states.jo: Jo masters her first impulse and welcomes the sacrifice.
states.meg: Meg covers and packs the breakfast immediately.
states.amy: Amy gives up the cream and muffins she most wanted.
states.beth: Beth asks to help carry food to the children.
states.hannah: Hannah helps ready the food and accompanies the family.

scenes.reason: Marmee enters and replaces breakfast with an urgent act of charity.

scenes.title: The Hummels’ Breakfast

states.marmee: Marmee brings food and aid into the freezing room and tends the sick mother.
states.jo: Jo jokes kindly with the frightened family and helps create warmth and cheer.
states.meg: Meg serves the family and recognizes the act as loving a neighbor.
states.amy: Amy gives her chosen delicacies to the hungry children.
states.beth: Beth helps feed and comfort the children.
states.hannah: Hannah carries wood, lights the fire, and blocks the broken windows.
states.mrsHummel: Mrs. Hummel receives the visitors with tearful gratitude.
states.hummelChildren: The hungry children eat, warm their hands, and call the March sisters angels.

scenes.reason: Travel to a new location adds the Hummel family and changes the sisters from recipients to providers.

scenes.title: Marmee’s Surprise

states.marmee: Marmee receives the daughters’ small gifts from the flower-decked chair of honor.
states.jo: Jo marshals the surprise and celebrates Marmee’s pleasure.
states.meg: Meg escorts Marmee with ceremony and shares the family affection.
states.amy: Amy opens the door for the presentation and explains her gift.
states.beth: Beth plays a march and offers her carefully marked handkerchiefs.

scenes.reason: The family returns home; the promised gift ceremony begins.

scenes.title: Preparing the Operatic Tragedy

states.jo: Jo builds scenery, manages effects, and prepares to play the principal male roles.
states.meg: Meg prepares costumes and the role of the witch Hagar.
states.amy: Amy prepares the fairy role despite limited dramatic skill.
states.beth: Beth arranges the piano music and supports the production.

scenes.reason: The day advances from gifts to physical preparation for the evening performance.

scenes.title: The Witches Curse

states.jo: Jo performs Hugo and Roderigo, improvising through collapsing scenery and tangled props.
states.meg: Meg plays Hagar and Don Pedro through the five-act melodrama.
states.amy: Amy plays Zara, falls with the improvised tower, and continues the melodrama despite the mishap.
states.beth: Beth helps the small company perform its music and supporting stage roles.
states.girlGuests: The invited girls form the audience, applaud the spectacle, and tumble when the cot closes.

scenes.reason: The audience arrives and the staged play becomes the active event.

scenes.title: Hannah Announces Supper

states.jo: Jo helps free the laughing audience from the collapsed cot after the final curtain.
states.meg: Meg joins the rescue while still dressed as Don Pedro.
states.amy: Amy remains with the actors as the audience recovers from its unexpected tumble.
states.beth: Beth stays with the little company after the play has ended.
states.girlGuests: The girls are taken unhurt from the folded cot and laugh at the accident.
states.hannah: Hannah enters with Mrs. March’s invitation to supper downstairs.

scenes.reason: The performance ends, the audience cot collapses, and Hannah physically enters to move the party downstairs.

scenes.title: Supper from Next Door

states.marmee: Marmee explains that Mr. Laurence sent the unexpected feast after hearing of the Hummel breakfast.
states.jo: Jo recognizes Laurie’s likely part in the gift and hopes to know him properly.
states.meg: Meg admires the flowers while considering the Laurence family.
states.amy: Amy marvels at the fairy-tale supper.
states.beth: Beth treasures Marmee’s preference for her modest roses and wishes Father could share Christmas.
states.girlGuests: The guests crowd around the surprise supper and discuss the neighbors.

scenes.reason: The play ends; an externally supplied supper and the Laurence household become the new subject.

chapters.title: THE LAURENCE BOY
chapters.notes: Read all 124 paragraphs. Mother’s actual farewell belongs to departure, not dressing. The dressing-room coaching begins at paragraph 35; dancing and the ankle report begin together in a single paragraph 92. Preserve the party’s shared setting and distinguish the carriage journey.

scenes.title: An Invitation in the Garret

states.jo: Jo reads in the garret, debates clothes and gloves, and agrees to attend the dance.
states.meg: Meg brings the invitation and plans how both sisters can appear respectably.

scenes.reason: Meg finds Jo alone in the garret and introduces the New Year’s Eve invitation.

scenes.title: Scorched Curls

states.jo: Jo overheats the curling tongs, burns Meg’s hair, and helps salvage both outfits.
states.meg: Meg mourns the lost curls, accepts the repair, and finishes dressing.
states.amy: Amy observes the disaster while attending the older sisters.
states.beth: Beth comforts Meg and helps the family complete the preparations.

scenes.reason: New Year’s Eve shifts to the bedrooms and the physical business of dressing.

scenes.title: Walking to the Gardiners

states.jo: Jo sets out and answers Mother’s last reminder about handkerchiefs.
states.meg: Meg leaves for the dance with a scented handkerchief and defends Mother’s standards.
states.marmee: Marmee gives the girls her farewell instructions and calls after them from the window.

scenes.reason: The sisters leave home and travel to the party.

scenes.title: Coaching in the Dressing Room

states.meg: Meg checks her sash and hair in Mrs. Gardiner’s mirror and coaches Jo on deportment.
states.jo: Jo asks Meg for a discreet signal if she forgets the rules of polite behavior.

scenes.reason: The sisters have arrived and stand in Mrs. Gardiner’s dressing room rather than on the road.

scenes.title: Jo Meets Laurie

states.jo: Jo retreats from the dance, recognizes the neighbor boy, and relaxes into candid conversation.
states.laurie: Laurie shelters from unfamiliar company, introduces himself by his preferred name, and tells Jo about school and travel.
states.meg: Meg dances in the adjoining rooms while Jo watches and praises her.
states.sallieGardiner: Sallie receives Meg into the party and helps her feel at ease.
states.partyGuests: The young guests gather, talk, and begin dancing while Jo looks for a quiet refuge.

scenes.reason: At the party Jo separates from Meg and directly meets Laurie.

scenes.title: Meg’s Turned Ankle

states.jo: Jo enjoys the polka with Laurie, then follows the injured Meg aside and tries to fetch refreshments.
states.meg: Meg rests in pain and hides the turned ankle until departure.
states.laurie: Laurie teaches Jo a German step, then offers coffee and ice when he finds her struggling.

scenes.reason: Meg’s injury changes the sisters’ goal from social enjoyment to managing a safe departure.

scenes.title: Laurie Arranges the Ride

states.jo: Jo accepts help after her attempts to manage the departure become impractical.
states.meg: Meg limps upstairs and reluctantly allows the injury to be disclosed.
states.laurie: Laurie serves the sisters and offers his grandfather’s carriage home.
states.hannah: Hannah arrives to escort the sisters and reluctantly accepts the carriage in the rain.
states.partyGuests: Two or three young guests join the quiet game of Buzz before Hannah arrives.

scenes.reason: Hannah arrives, and Laurie converts the private difficulty into a travel plan.

scenes.title: The Carriage Home

states.jo: Jo relaxes in the carriage and recounts her evening with Laurie.
states.meg: Meg describes her dancing and invitation to the Moffats despite her aching ankle.
states.laurie: Laurie conveys the sisters and Hannah home through the rain.
states.hannah: Hannah rides home with the young people after accepting Laurie’s help.

scenes.reason: The cast changes location and reviews the night during travel.

scenes.title: Bonbons After Midnight

states.jo: Jo gives the younger girls saved bonbons and tells the most exciting parts of the party.
states.meg: Meg rests in her dressing gown and concludes that finery added little to their happiness.
states.amy: Amy wakes to demand the party story and listens over the sweets.
states.beth: Beth wakes with Amy and eagerly hears the adventures.

scenes.reason: The sisters return home; Laurie and Hannah leave, and the younger sisters become present.

chapters.title: BURDENS
chapters.notes: Read all 70 paragraphs. Separate the upstairs opening, the downstairs breakfast, Amy’s conversation with Meg, and the shifts among the evening’s reports. Correct Meg’s Kings story and Beth’s account of Mr. Laurence’s fish gift.

scenes.title: A Cross Morning

states.meg: Meg chooses between shabby gowns and resents returning to work after the holiday.
states.jo: Jo jokes about carrying Aunt March as a burden and urges a more cheerful start.

scenes.reason: The holiday ends with the whole household directly present and out of temper.

scenes.title: A Household Out of Sorts

states.jo: Jo loses her temper after spilling ink, breaking her laces, and sitting on her hat.
states.meg: Meg threatens to banish the kittens after one clings to her dress.
states.beth: Beth nurses her headache on the sofa and begs for the kittens.
states.amy: Amy cries over the wrong arithmetic sum and cannot find her rubbers.
states.marmee: Marmee struggles to finish an urgent letter amid the household racket.
states.hannah: Hannah enters with the hot turnovers despite her own bad temper.

scenes.reason: Meg comes downstairs and the full household becomes directly present at breakfast.

scenes.title: Shouldering the Bundles

states.jo: Jo walks into the winter wind, jokes Meg out of her injured mood, and parts for Aunt March’s house.
states.meg: Meg walks toward the Kings under a heavy veil and lets Jo’s nonsense restore her humor.

scenes.reason: Meg and Jo leave the house together, then separate for their different work.

scenes.title: Meg at the Kings

states.meg: Meg works as nursery governess, values her small wage, and wrestles with envy of the wealthy household around her.
states.kingChildren: The four spoiled King children occupy Meg through the working day.

scenes.reason: The narration follows Meg to her distinct workplace and burden.

scenes.title: Jo and Aunt March

states.jo: Jo waits on her demanding great-aunt and escapes into the library whenever duty permits.
states.auntMarch: Aunt March scolds, lectures, and dozes while testing Jo’s temper.

scenes.reason: The narration moves to Jo’s separate place of work and her recurring contest of wills.

scenes.title: Beth’s Quiet Work

states.beth: Beth studies at home, keeps house with Hannah, tends her dolls, and privately bears the work and shyness that trouble her.
states.hannah: Hannah teaches Beth household tasks and shares the daily work.

scenes.reason: The narrative moves home to Beth’s distinct routine and burden.

scenes.title: Amy at School

states.amy: Amy cultivates art and manners at school while vanity, imitation, and fear of public disgrace shape her days.
states.schoolGirls: Amy’s schoolfellows form the audience whose approval and ridicule matter intensely to her.

scenes.reason: The narrator describes Amy’s school habits and classmates before returning to her conversation with Meg.

scenes.title: Amy Confides in Meg

states.amy: Amy tells Meg that her flat nose and borrowed purple dress are trials she must bear.
states.meg: Meg receives Amy’s confidence and serves as her older-sister monitor.

scenes.reason: A direct sisterly confidence replaces the narrator’s school profile; the schoolmates are absent.

scenes.title: Stories After Work

states.jo: Jo recounts persuading Aunt March to enjoy The Vicar of Wakefield instead of Belsham.
states.meg: Meg asks whether Aunt March admitted liking the livelier book.
states.beth: Beth sews beside the family while Jo recounts the afternoon’s contest over reading.
states.amy: Amy hears Jo’s comic report as the sisters sew together.
states.marmee: Marmee listens to Jo’s account in the family’s evening sewing circle.

scenes.reason: The separated family regathers and compares the day’s experiences under Marmee’s guidance.

scenes.title: Lessons from the Kings and School

states.meg: Meg reports finding the Kings distressed by their son’s disgrace and values her own family’s security.
states.amy: Amy describes Susie’s public punishment and renounces her envy of the carnelian ring.
states.jo: Jo asks whether the pupils laughed at Susie’s caricature of Mr. Davis.
states.beth: Beth listens to the two accounts while arranging Jo’s sewing basket.
states.marmee: Marmee hears the daughters compare wealth, envy, and disgrace.

scenes.reason: Jo’s comic story ends and Meg and Amy share distinct reports that change their judgments.

scenes.title: The Fish-shop Kindness

states.beth: Beth recounts seeing Mr. Laurence give a poor woman a large fish when the fishmonger refused work.
states.jo: Jo hears Beth’s account while her sister puts the topsy-turvy basket in order.
states.meg: Meg listens with the family to Beth’s account of the unexpected generosity.
states.amy: Amy hears the story of the poor woman’s grateful response.
states.marmee: Marmee listens before the family asks for a story of her own.

scenes.reason: Beth becomes the storyteller and supplies a new observed example of poverty and kindness.

scenes.title: A Father’s Four Sons

states.marmee: Marmee recounts meeting the father who freely gave four sons to the war and feeling ashamed of her own fear.
states.jo: Jo listens to Mother’s account, then asks for another real story with a moral.
states.meg: Meg hears the cost borne by the old soldier’s father while the sewing circle grows sober.
states.amy: Amy listens as Mother contrasts her own worries with the stranger’s sacrifices.
states.beth: Beth hears Mother explain why she gave the tired father clothing and money.

scenes.reason: Mother replaces Beth as storyteller and the wartime testimony changes the circle’s emotional weight.

scenes.title: Counting Their Blessings

states.marmee: Marmee turns the daughters’ own reports into a fable about gratitude.
states.jo: Jo sees the point and adds a comic reminder to count their mercies.
states.meg: Meg recognizes the sermon hidden in the promised romance.
states.beth: Beth approves the kind of lesson Father used to tell.
states.amy: Amy claims her warning from Susie’s disgrace and promises to complain less.

scenes.reason: Jo requests another story, and Mother converts the preceding accounts into a new shared resolve.

chapters.title: BEING NEIGHBORLY
chapters.notes: Read all 135 paragraphs. Distinguish the hall, Jo’s solo snow clearing, the window conversation across properties, the maid’s direct entrances, the conservatory, and the final hall farewell. No absent March sister becomes a sickroom visitor.

scenes.title: A Path Through the Snow

states.jo: Jo comes through the hall with broom and shovel and declares that she wants an adventure.
states.meg: Meg urges Jo to stay warm by the fire rather than seek more exercise.

scenes.reason: Jo leaves the shared room, begins outdoor work, and forms a new goal.

scenes.title: Jo Clears the Garden Paths

states.jo: Jo sweeps paths for Beth’s dolls, recalls Laurie watching the garden, and sees him at the upper window.

scenes.reason: Meg goes back to her book indoors, leaving Jo to outdoor work and the remembered plan for a visit.

scenes.title: A Snowball at the Window

states.jo: Jo throws a snowball to catch Laurie’s attention and offers to visit if Marmee permits.
states.laurie: Laurie opens the window after a week of illness and eagerly accepts Jo’s offer of company.

scenes.reason: Laurie appears at the window and the neighbors make a direct plan.

scenes.title: Preparing for a Visitor

states.jo: Jo heads indoors after promising to ask permission for the visit.
states.laurie: Laurie brushes his hair, changes his collar, and tidies the room in eager anticipation.
states.laurenceMaid: A surprised servant comes upstairs to announce the young lady.

scenes.reason: The invitation is settled; one source paragraph follows Jo’s departure and the preparations in Laurie’s room.

scenes.title: Bag and Baggage

states.jo: Jo arrives with blancmange, kittens, and family greetings, sets the sickroom straight, and talks without ceremony.
states.laurie: Laurie welcomes Jo into his private parlor, laughs away his bashfulness, and admits how lonely the neighboring family can make him feel.

scenes.reason: Jo enters the Laurence house and becomes Laurie’s visitor and nurse.

scenes.title: Laughter in the Sickroom

states.jo: Jo delights Laurie with the story of Aunt March’s suitor and continues the family tales.
states.laurie: Laurie laughs until he cries, asks for more, and discovers Jo shares his love of books.
states.laurenceMaid: The maid looks in to discover the cause of Laurie’s unusually loud laughter.

scenes.reason: The maid physically appears at the laughter, changing the direct cast before the tour.

scenes.title: The Enchanted House

states.jo: Jo follows Laurie through the house and delights in the well-stocked library.
states.laurie: Laurie shows Jo the rooms and confesses that books cannot replace companionship.

scenes.reason: Jo and Laurie tour the mansion and settle in its library; the doctor’s summons comes in the following event.

scenes.title: The Doctor Calls

states.laurenceMaid: The maid announces the doctor and beckons Laurie away.
states.laurie: Laurie asks Jo to excuse him and leaves to see the doctor.
states.jo: Jo stays happily in the library and studies the grandfather’s portrait alone.

scenes.reason: The maid enters with the summons and Laurie departs; Jo’s private examination of the portrait precedes the grandfather’s answer.

scenes.title: Jo Meets the Lion

states.jo: Jo is caught studying a portrait, answers the formidable grandfather honestly, and explains her neighborly visit.
states.mrLaurence: Mr. Laurence overhears Jo, tests her candor, and warms to her account of Laurie and the Hummels.

scenes.reason: Laurie departs for the doctor and Mr. Laurence enters, changing the present cast and stakes.

scenes.title: Tea with the Laurences

states.jo: Jo takes Mr. Laurence’s arm to tea and chats naturally once Laurie joins them.
states.laurie: Laurie rushes downstairs, then shares an easy tea with Jo under his grandfather’s watch.
states.mrLaurence: Mr. Laurence observes the young people and decides that the March sisters may ease Laurie’s loneliness.

scenes.reason: The doctor visit ends and all three gather at the tea table.

scenes.title: Flowers in the Conservatory

states.jo: Jo walks through the lighted conservatory enjoying its warmth and flowers.
states.laurie: Laurie cuts a bouquet for Marmee and thanks her for the medicine she sent.

scenes.reason: Tea ends and the two young people leave Mr. Laurence for the conservatory.

scenes.title: Music in the Drawing Room

states.jo: Jo admires the piano, listens for Beth’s sake, and notices Mr. Laurence’s displeasure at the music.
states.laurie: Laurie plays for Jo but stops when his grandfather calls the pleasure excessive.
states.mrLaurence: Mr. Laurence listens briefly, interrupts, and arranges for John to escort Jo home.

scenes.reason: Jo and Laurie return from the conservatory to the drawing room, where Mr. Laurence is standing by the fire.

scenes.title: A Promise to Visit

states.jo: Jo asks in the hall why Grandfather disliked the music and promises another visit.
states.laurie: Laurie explains his grandfather’s dislike, offers John as escort, and promises to visit the Marches.

scenes.reason: Jo and Laurie move into the hall and speak privately after leaving the grandfather.

scenes.title: The Afternoon Retold

states.jo: Jo recounts every adventure and defends a straightforward friendship with Laurie.
states.meg: Meg reads romance into Laurie’s manners and teases Jo about his compliment.
states.amy: Amy insists she is nearly old enough to judge the new friendship.
states.beth: Beth thinks of the lions before Palace Beautiful and the courage friendship will require.
states.marmee: Marmee explains the old musical hurt and welcomes Laurie as a neighbor.

scenes.reason: Jo returns home; the March family replaces the Laurence cast and interprets the visit.

chapters.title: BETH FINDS THE PALACE BEAUTIFUL
chapters.notes: Read all 44 paragraphs. Treat the two-household overview as narration, isolate Grandfather’s instruction to Brooke, and distinguish Beth’s piano visits from the unseen listeners. The final sisters see the escort at the March gate, not the earlier kiss inside the study.

scenes.title: The Palace Opens
scenes.reason: A narrated interval establishes the two households’ new shared routine and Beth’s remaining barrier.

scenes.title: Grandfather Grants a Holiday

states.mrLaurence: Mr. Laurence tells Brooke to let Laurie enjoy the Marches’ company and make up his studies afterward.
states.mrBrooke: Brooke receives Grandfather’s permission after reporting Laurie’s repeated truancy.

scenes.reason: The narrated overview narrows to Grandfather’s direct response to the tutor’s reports.

scenes.title: Kindness Between Two Houses
scenes.reason: A montage across both homes has no single physical gathering.

scenes.title: An Invitation for the Musical Girl

states.beth: Beth listens breathlessly and finally thanks Mr. Laurence for permission to use the piano unseen.
states.mrLaurence: Mr. Laurence carefully presents the unused piano as a favor Beth could do him.
states.marmee: Marmee receives Mr. Laurence and watches his tact bring Beth past her fear.

scenes.reason: Mr. Laurence visits the March home with a request crafted specifically for Beth.

scenes.title: Beth at the Great Piano

states.beth: Beth slips through the hedge, plays alone for hours, and returns radiant from the music she had feared to approach.

scenes.reason: Beth crosses into the Laurence house and begins the private musical visits.

scenes.title: Hannah Collects Beth

states.beth: Beth ends her long first piano visit so delighted that she has no appetite for dinner.
states.hannah: Hannah comes to collect Beth and take her home to dinner.

scenes.reason: Hannah physically arrives after Beth’s solitary playing.

scenes.title: Music Heard Unseen

states.beth: Beth plays the new music without knowing that either Laurence is protecting her privacy.
states.mrLaurence: Mr. Laurence opens his study door to listen unseen to the familiar airs.
states.laurie: Laurie stands guard in the hall to keep the servants from disturbing Beth.

scenes.reason: The later routine explicitly places the player and the two unseen helpers in different rooms.

scenes.title: Slippers for Mr. Laurence

states.beth: Beth asks Mother’s permission to embroider slippers as a thank-you gift.
states.marmee: Marmee approves the gift and offers to pay for making up the slippers.

scenes.reason: Gratitude becomes a concrete household project after Beth’s repeated visits.

scenes.title: The Slippers Reach the Study
scenes.reason: One source paragraph spans the planning, weeks of sewing, and a later secret delivery; no simultaneous group is invented.

scenes.title: The Little Piano Arrives

states.beth: Beth enters in suspense, is overwhelmed by the piano and letter, and lets Jo read for her.
states.jo: Jo ushers Beth to the gift, reads Mr. Laurence’s letter, and explains his tenderness toward the child he lost.
states.meg: Meg celebrates the gift and examines its details with her sisters.
states.amy: Amy admires the formal letter and decorative instrument.
states.hannah: Hannah urges Beth to play and shares the family’s wonder.

scenes.reason: A delivery transforms the parlor and brings the household together around Mr. Laurence’s gift.

scenes.title: Beth Thanks Him Herself

states.beth: Beth crosses the hedge without escort, thanks Mr. Laurence, and kisses him with fearless gratitude.
states.mrLaurence: Mr. Laurence receives Beth’s embrace in astonishment and holds her as he once held his granddaughter.

scenes.reason: Beth undertakes an unprecedented visit and directly meets the man she once feared.

scenes.title: The Escort at the Gate

states.jo: Jo dances a jig when she sees Mr. Laurence escort Beth to their gate.
states.amy: Amy nearly falls from the window in surprise at Beth’s new confidence.
states.meg: Meg throws up her hands at the sight of the formal escort.
states.beth: Beth comes home beside Mr. Laurence without her old fear.
states.mrLaurence: Mr. Laurence escorts Beth to her gate, shakes her hand, and raises his hat.

scenes.reason: The viewpoint returns to the March sisters watching the completed change in Beth.

chapters.title: AMY’S VALLEY OF HUMILIATION
chapters.notes: Read all 59 paragraphs. Laurie praises Beth, not Jo. Separate confiscation from the ferrule, home comfort from Jo’s return to school, and the evening’s changes in cast. Meg and Hannah are directly shown during the afternoon comfort, not in the later chess conversation.

scenes.title: The Lime Fashion

states.amy: Amy explains the school economy of pickled limes and asks for help clearing her debts.
states.jo: Jo laughs at Amy’s verbal mistakes and challenges the importance of the fashion.
states.meg: Meg questions the debt, then gives Amy a quarter with a warning to make it last.

scenes.reason: Amy’s school problem becomes a concrete family decision before the school day.

scenes.title: Contraband in the Desk

states.amy: Amy displays her limes, distributes them among her circle, and withholds one from a taunting classmate.
states.schoolGirls: The pupils trade, admire, and compete over Amy’s newly restored supply.
states.mrDavis: Mr. Davis hears Jenny’s report of Amy’s limes and angrily calls the school to order.

scenes.reason: The action moves to school and the forbidden purchase becomes public among the pupils.

scenes.title: Before the Whole School

states.amy: Amy surrenders the hidden limes and carries them to the window under the class’s eyes.
states.mrDavis: Mr. Davis orders every lime thrown into the street despite the pupils’ appeals.
states.schoolGirls: The pupils sigh and watch their hoped-for feast fall to the children outside.

scenes.reason: Mr. Davis calls the school to order and turns the private contraband into formal punishment.

scenes.title: The Ferrule and the Platform

states.amy: Amy bears the blows without pleading and stands humiliated before the class.
states.mrDavis: Mr. Davis enforces his promised punishment and sends Amy to the platform until recess.
states.schoolGirls: The girls watch Amy’s white, motionless figure and struggle to return to their lessons.

scenes.reason: The confiscation ends and punishment changes to bodily pain and public disgrace.

scenes.title: Comfort for the Insulted Hand

states.amy: Amy leaves school and returns home devastated by the punishment.
states.meg: Meg bathes Amy’s hand with glycerine and tears.
states.beth: Beth feels that even her kittens cannot console Amy’s grief.
states.jo: Jo proposes having the teacher arrested.
states.marmee: Marmee comforts Amy tenderly while keeping her own disturbance quiet.
states.hannah: Hannah shakes her fist and pounds the dinner potatoes as though they were Mr. Davis.

scenes.reason: Amy leaves school and the whole family becomes directly present in the home response.

scenes.title: Jo Collects Amy’s Property

states.jo: Jo delivers Mother’s letter, gathers Amy’s belongings, and scrapes her boots on departure.
states.mrDavis: Mr. Davis receives Jo’s grim visit after an unusually nervous afternoon.
states.schoolGirls: The pupils observe the teacher’s changed manner and Jo’s arrival before school closes.

scenes.reason: The next paragraph returns physically to school with Jo rather than Amy.

scenes.title: A Vacation from Mr. Davis

states.amy: Amy learns she may leave Mr. Davis’s school but must still study with Beth.
states.marmee: Marmee rejects corporal punishment while explaining why Amy’s disobedience deserved correction.
states.jo: Jo plays chess with Laurie while listening to Mother’s judgment of Amy’s conduct.
states.laurie: Laurie plays chess in the corner as Mother speaks to Amy.
states.beth: Beth stands near the chess players during the family’s evening discussion.

scenes.reason: Amy returns home; the family and Laurie assess both the punishment and its lesson.

scenes.title: A Compliment for Beth

states.laurie: Laurie praises the musical girl without naming Beth and then makes his meaning clear.
states.beth: Beth blushes and hides her face when she realizes Laurie means her own music.
states.jo: Jo lets Laurie win the game in gratitude for his praise of Beth.
states.amy: Amy hears Laurie’s modest account of an unadvertised talent.
states.marmee: Marmee’s lesson about modest gifts receives Laurie’s concrete example.

scenes.reason: Laurie’s intervention creates a new discovery for Beth and changes the chess game’s emotional meaning.

scenes.title: Laurie’s Music and Departure

states.laurie: Laurie sings for the household after Beth declines to play, then goes home.
states.beth: Beth cannot be persuaded to perform after the unexpected compliment.
states.jo: Jo remains with the family as the chess evening gives way to Laurie’s singing.
states.amy: Amy thinks quietly, then asks after Laurie leaves whether he is accomplished.
states.marmee: Marmee stays with Amy as the evening visitor departs.

scenes.reason: The game ends, Laurie sings, and his departure leads Amy to a fresh question.

scenes.title: Learning Modesty

states.amy: Amy works out that accomplishments are pleasing when they are not displayed conceitedly.
states.marmee: Marmee explains that Laurie’s education and modesty can be seen without ostentation.
states.jo: Jo compares showing off every accomplishment to wearing all one’s gowns and ribbons together.
states.beth: Beth remains in the evening circle as Mother and Amy draw the lesson from the compliment.

scenes.reason: Laurie is gone; Mother, Amy, and Jo interpret his example without giving him another presence snapshot.

chapters.title: JO MEETS APOLLYON
chapters.notes: Read all 91 paragraphs. The skating advice comes from Meg, not Beth. Separate the evening return from next-day discovery, Marmee’s later arrival from Jo’s violence, and Jo’s solitary resentment from the follow-up conversation. Keep the warning, rescue, moral counsel, and reconciliation distinct.

scenes.title: Not Invited

states.amy: Amy discovers the theater plan, demands to join it, and promises Jo she will be sorry when excluded.
states.jo: Jo refuses to alter Laurie’s invitation and leaves with anger sharpened by Amy’s persistence.
states.meg: Meg tries to soften the refusal but follows Jo when Laurie calls from below.

scenes.reason: Amy interrupts Meg and Jo while they dress and demands inclusion in the theater plan.

scenes.title: Amy’s Last Warning

states.amy: Amy cries on the floor and threatens Jo from above the banisters.
states.meg: Meg leaves the bedroom after trying to reason with Amy.
states.jo: Jo dismisses Amy’s warning and slams the door on departure.
states.laurie: Laurie calls the invited sisters from downstairs before the theater outing.

scenes.reason: Laurie becomes directly audible from below and the older sisters leave the room.

scenes.title: The Seven Castles

states.jo: Jo enjoys the brilliant spectacle with Laurie and Meg, dismissing Amy’s threat.
states.meg: Meg shares the theater outing while hoping the quarrel will pass.
states.laurie: Laurie hosts the invited sisters for the performance.

scenes.reason: The invited party leaves home and attends the play without Amy.

scenes.title: Home from the Theater

states.amy: Amy reads with an injured air and refuses to ask about the play.
states.beth: Beth asks the returning sisters for a description of the spectacle.
states.meg: Meg returns from the play and helps answer Beth’s eager questions.
states.jo: Jo checks her room and mistakenly concludes that Amy has forgiven the quarrel.

scenes.reason: The party returns that night, before the manuscript loss is discovered the following afternoon.

scenes.title: The Burned Manuscript

states.amy: Amy reveals that she burned Jo’s cherished handwritten book in revenge and is shaken by Jo’s fury.
states.jo: Jo discovers the loss, strikes and shakes Amy, and declares that she will never forgive her.
states.meg: Meg rescues Amy and tries to restrain Jo.
states.beth: Beth attempts to calm Jo during the outburst.

scenes.reason: The next day Jo discovers the promised retaliation; the family crisis becomes physical.

scenes.title: Marmee Hears of the Manuscript

states.marmee: Marmee comes home, hears the story, and makes Amy understand the wrong she has done.
states.amy: Amy regrets destroying Jo’s painstaking fair copy and knows she must ask forgiveness.
states.beth: Beth mourns Jo’s manuscript as she would a lost kitten.
states.meg: Meg refuses to excuse Amy’s revenge.

scenes.reason: Jo has gone to the garret; Mother arrives downstairs after the violence.

scenes.title: Anger at Sundown

states.amy: Amy apologizes at tea and retreats into renewed resentment when Jo rejects her.
states.jo: Jo refuses Amy’s apology and resists Marmee’s warning not to carry anger into night.
states.marmee: Marmee quietly warns Jo that delay will make forgiveness harder.
states.meg: Meg sings with Mother after the quarrel leaves the other voices silent.
states.beth: Beth plays the accompaniment while Jo refuses to sing and Amy breaks down.

scenes.reason: At tea Amy attempts reconciliation, but Jo chooses to preserve the grievance.

scenes.title: Another Day of Resentment
scenes.reason: A narrated day ranges across work, street, and home rather than depicting one shared gathering.

scenes.title: Jo Seeks Laurie

states.jo: Jo decides skating with Laurie may restore her good temper and goes to ask him.

scenes.reason: Jo makes a concrete new decision and leaves before Amy seeks advice.

scenes.title: Amy Runs After Them

states.amy: Amy sees Jo going skating, accepts Meg’s advice, and hurries to follow.
states.meg: Meg urges Amy to wait for Jo’s temper to improve and offer a quiet kiss or kindness.

scenes.reason: The next morning Amy forms a new plan after seeing the skaters depart.

scenes.title: Thin Ice

states.jo: Jo hears Laurie’s warning but deliberately leaves Amy uninformed until the ice breaks beneath her.
states.amy: Amy struggles onto her skates, follows toward the smoother middle, and falls through the thin ice.
states.laurie: Laurie tests the river ahead, warns Jo to stay near shore, and races back to direct the rescue.

scenes.reason: All three reach the river; Jo’s sustained anger becomes immediate physical danger.

scenes.title: The Rescue

states.jo: Jo obeys Laurie blindly, reaches Amy with a rail, and hauls her from the water.
states.amy: Amy clings to the rail and is pulled shivering from the broken ice.
states.laurie: Laurie directs the rescue, frees himself from his skates, and organizes the fastest return home.

scenes.reason: Amy breaks through, changing the event from pursuit to rescue.

scenes.title: Jo’s Bosom Enemy

states.jo: Jo shows her bruised, cut hands to Mother and confesses the resentment that almost cost Amy her life.
states.amy: Amy sleeps safely in blankets after being brought home from the ice.
states.marmee: Marmee binds Jo’s hurt hands and urges her to watch and pray against her temper.

scenes.reason: Amy is safely home; the physical emergency gives way to Jo’s moral reckoning and reconciliation.

scenes.title: Marmee’s Own Temper

states.marmee: Marmee admits her own lifelong anger and explains the habits and faith that help her control it.
states.jo: Jo is astonished by Mother’s confession and draws comfort from their shared struggle.
states.amy: Amy sleeps through the private counsel while recovering from the fright.

scenes.reason: Mother’s admission changes Jo’s knowledge and turns remorse toward a practical lifelong discipline.

scenes.title: The Sisters Reconcile

states.amy: Amy wakes, smiles, and reaches for Jo without another word of reproach.
states.jo: Jo strokes Amy’s wet hair and answers her outstretched arms with a forgiving embrace.
states.marmee: Marmee remains beside the bed after guiding Jo toward reconciliation.

scenes.reason: Amy wakes; spoken remorse gives way to the sisters’ direct physical reconciliation.

chapters.title: MEG GOES TO VANITY FAIR
chapters.notes: Read all 143 paragraphs, including the complete dress-making paragraph. Mother’s gifts are reported during packing, not delivered there. Separate the bouquet in the dressing room from the first party, include Mrs. Moffat’s direct gossip, and correct which sister coaches the borrowed costume.

scenes.title: Packing for the Moffats

states.meg: Meg packs borrowed ribbons and her best modest clothes while struggling against envy of fashionable things.
states.jo: Jo helps prepare Meg and challenges each new wish for luxury.
states.beth: Beth sorts and lends ribbons while reminding Meg of her earlier contentment.
states.amy: Amy arranges Meg’s belongings and imagines the pleasures of going herself.

scenes.reason: The family prepares Meg for a two-week visit and names the temptation she is about to face.

scenes.title: A Fortnight of Novelty

states.meg: Meg enters the Moffats’ fashionable routine and compares her limited wardrobe with her hosts’ abundance.
states.annieMoffat: Annie welcomes Meg into days of shopping, visiting, and evening entertainment.
states.sallieGardiner: Sallie joins the young women’s round of pleasures.
states.mrsMoffat: Mrs. Moffat welcomes Meg warmly and joins the household’s affectionate attention to its guest.

scenes.reason: Meg leaves home and enters the Moffat household for an extended visit.

scenes.title: Flowers in the Dressing Room

states.meg: Meg is ashamed of the old dress until Mother’s note and Laurie’s flowers restore her spirits.
states.annieMoffat: Annie opens the flower box eagerly and helps Meg tie her sash.
states.belleMoffat: Belle praises Meg’s arms and joins the surprise at her bouquet.
states.claraMoffat: Clara calls Meg sweet after receiving a prettily shared bouquet.
states.sallieGardiner: Sallie offers to arrange Meg’s hair beside her own crisp new dress.
states.moffatMaid: The maid brings Meg’s flower box and the accompanying note.

scenes.reason: The first party turns private insecurity into public gossip about Meg and Laurie.

scenes.title: Gossip Behind the Flowers

states.meg: Meg dances and sings happily, then hears the humiliating speculation about her mother and Laurie.
states.annieMoffat: Annie persuades Meg to sing for the party.
states.mrsMoffat: Mrs. Moffat joins the discussion of a supposed Laurence match and Meg’s poor dress.
states.mrMoffat: Mr. Moffat insists on dancing with Meg because she moves so energetically.
states.partyGuests: The company dances, compliments Meg, and speculates about her place in society.

scenes.reason: The dressing-room gift scene ends; the public party and overheard marriage gossip begin.

scenes.title: A Joke About Mr. Laurence

states.meg: Meg wakes troubled, then parries the sisters’ teasing by pretending their invitation concerns Laurie’s grandfather.
states.annieMoffat: Annie questions Meg about the young Laurence and her supposed intimacy.
states.belleMoffat: Belle tries to draw Meg into talk of a possible admirer.
states.claraMoffat: Clara joins Belle in treating Meg’s friendship as a romantic opportunity.

scenes.reason: The morning after the overheard gossip, Meg must answer insinuations directly.

scenes.title: Belle’s Offer

states.meg: Meg admits she owns no second party dress and accepts Belle’s offer to transform her appearance.
states.belleMoffat: Belle offers clothes, ornaments, and her maid’s skill as an experiment in dressing Meg.
states.sallieGardiner: Sallie innocently exposes Meg’s lack of another gown and encourages the makeover.
states.mrsMoffat: Mrs. Moffat offers errands for the young guests before going out.

scenes.reason: Preparations for the larger party force Meg to choose whether to borrow a fashionable identity.

scenes.title: Dressed as a Doll

states.meg: Meg submits to powder, tight curls, a low dress, jewelry, and practiced manners, then enters the party unlike herself.
states.belleMoffat: Belle directs the transformation and presents Meg as her successful creation.
states.hortense: Hortense alters Meg’s hair, complexion, and dress.
states.annieMoffat: Annie is asked to coach Meg in managing the long skirt and French heels.
states.sallieGardiner: Sallie praises the transformed Meg while trying not to mind being outshone.
states.claraMoffat: Clara is asked to pin back Meg’s long curl with her silver butterfly.

scenes.reason: The makeover begins physically and changes Meg’s appearance and behavior.

scenes.title: Laurie Does Not Know Her

states.meg: Meg performs her borrowed elegance, feels exposed by adult gossip, and asks Laurie to approve the result.
states.laurie: Laurie arrives to report for Jo, dislikes the disguise, and bluntly says Meg no longer looks like herself.
states.partyGuests: The fashionable company watches and discusses Meg as a possible match.
states.mrsMoffat: Mrs. Moffat exaggerates Meg’s family position and speaks of Ned’s admiration.
states.belleMoffat: Belle nudges Annie when Meg and Laurie notice each other.
states.annieMoffat: Annie exchanges a knowing look with Belle at Laurie’s arrival.

scenes.reason: Meg enters the crowded party and Laurie becomes a direct witness to the transformation.

scenes.title: Fuss and Feathers

states.meg: Meg overhears herself called a spoiled little girl, regrets the disguise, then reconciles with Laurie over a dance.
states.laurie: Laurie apologizes for his bluntness, dances with Meg, and agrees to keep her confidence.
states.partyGuests: Nearby adults criticize the makeover while the dance continues.

scenes.reason: Adult criticism confirms Laurie’s judgment and shifts Meg from pride to regret.

scenes.title: The Doll’s Last Dances

states.meg: Meg asks Laurie for silence, drinks champagne, flirts, and pushes the borrowed role until a headache and shame replace pleasure.
states.laurie: Laurie gives his word, warns Meg against the champagne, and withdraws unhappily.
states.nedMoffat: Ned claims his dances and encourages the party behavior Meg imitates.
states.fisher: Fisher accompanies Ned at supper and stoops to pick up Meg’s fan.

scenes.reason: Meg chooses to continue the performance after recognizing its cost.

scenes.title: Meg Confesses

states.meg: Meg returns home, confesses the disguise and flirtation, and reports the humiliating marriage gossip.
states.marmee: Marmee listens without ridicule, rejects matchmaking plans, and explains the character and work she values for her daughters.
states.jo: Jo hears Meg’s confession, rages at the gossip, and accepts Marmee’s vision of honorable independence.

scenes.reason: Back home, Meg replaces her cheerful travel report with the truth she withheld from the younger sisters.

chapters.title: THE P.C. AND P.O.
chapters.notes: Read all 85 paragraphs, including every inserted newspaper article, poem, notice, and report. Meg is Pickwick and reads the Portfolio; Jo is Snodgrass and edits it. The text’s fictional Venetian cast remains inside the newspaper and is not imported as physical participants. Separate the garden opening and later postal coda.

scenes.title: The Four Garden Plots

states.meg: Meg tends a plot of roses, heliotrope, myrtle, and a little orange tree.
states.jo: Jo plans a changing sunflower plantation whose seeds will feed the chickens.
states.beth: Beth grows fragrant old-fashioned flowers and plants for the pets.
states.amy: Amy cultivates a picturesque bower of vines, lilies, ferns, and bright plants.

scenes.reason: The chapter first describes the sisters’ distinct garden plots, before moving to the rainy-day club.

scenes.title: The Pickwick Portfolio

states.meg: Meg presides as Samuel Pickwick and reads the club’s newspaper through her glassless spectacles.
states.jo: Jo plays Augustus Snodgrass, edits the newspaper, and tilts back in her chair until Meg corrects her.
states.beth: Beth takes the role of Tracy Tupman and listens to the club’s stories and notices.
states.amy: Amy plays Nathaniel Winkle and hears her own contribution and its punctuation warning.

scenes.reason: The chapter opens inside the sisters’ established literary club and reproduces its newspaper.

scenes.title: A New Member Proposed

states.jo: Jo proposes Laurie’s admission, argues for his honor, and forces a formal vote.
states.meg: Meg fears a boy will laugh at the paper but conducts the vote as president.
states.beth: Beth overcomes her reserve and votes to admit Laurie out of gratitude.
states.amy: Amy objects to boys disturbing the club, then joins the majority.

scenes.reason: The reading ends and Jo introduces a real change to the club’s membership.

scenes.title: Sam Weller and the Post Office

states.jo: Jo reveals Laurie from the cupboard and applauds the secret plan.
states.laurie: Laurie accepts the club name Sam Weller and presents the hedge post office as his contribution.
states.meg: Meg rebukes the conspirators before welcoming Laurie’s useful scheme.
states.beth: Beth accepts the new member and the prospect of private correspondence.
states.amy: Amy forgives the trick when the post office promises notes and parcels.

scenes.reason: Laurie becomes physically present and converts admission into a lasting institution.

scenes.title: The Club and Its Post Flourish
scenes.reason: The meeting has adjourned; a later narrated montage is not another simultaneous gathering in the garret.

chapters.title: EXPERIMENTS
chapters.notes: Read all 83 paragraphs. Distinguish the week-long montage, Mother upstairs, Jo’s solo kitchen, Sallie’s earlier call, Miss Crocker’s actual dinner attendance, the funeral, the divided chores and drive, and the evening porch. Jo carries the tray; the failed breakfast is omelet and biscuits, not hard eggs. Beth lays Pip to rest but does not sing the epitaph.

scenes.title: Fun Forever

states.meg: Meg proposes sleeping late and doing nothing during her vacation.
states.jo: Jo plans unrestricted reading and outings with Laurie.
states.amy: Amy asks to abandon lessons and play through the holiday.
states.beth: Beth agrees to rest while imagining music and dolls instead of duties.
states.marmee: Marmee permits a one-week experiment and predicts that all play will become burdensome.

scenes.reason: The sisters jointly choose their experiment under Marmee’s observation.

scenes.title: A Week of Idleness
scenes.reason: The proposed holiday becomes a narrated week whose accumulating disorder changes every sister’s state.

scenes.title: No Breakfast

states.meg: Meg discovers Marmee resting and assumes command of the unfamiliar household work.
states.jo: Jo welcomes the novelty before confronting the cold stove and missing meal.
states.amy: Amy joins the improvised work without practical skill.
states.beth: Beth searches the disordered house with her sisters.

scenes.reason: Saturday removes Marmee and Hannah’s invisible labor, making the experiment’s cost immediate.

scenes.title: Bitter Tea and Scorched Omelet

states.meg: Meg presides over the teapot while the sisters attempt their first unaided breakfast.
states.jo: Jo works beside Meg and offers to carry Mother’s tray upstairs.
states.amy: Amy attempts to help with the meal and endures its failures.
states.beth: Beth shares the work and the discouraging breakfast.

scenes.reason: The sisters attempt their first replacement duty and experience a concrete failure.

scenes.title: Mother’s Breakfast Tray

states.jo: Jo delivers the unpalatable breakfast to Mother with the cooks’ compliments.
states.marmee: Marmee thanks Jo, then privately replaces the spoiled breakfast with her own provisions.

scenes.reason: The tray goes upstairs; Mother is physically shown in her own room, not in the kitchen.

scenes.title: Jo Invites a Dinner Guest

states.jo: Jo volunteers to cook dinner, invites Laurie, and describes an ambitious menu.
states.meg: Meg tidies the parlor, warns Jo against too many dishes, and urges her to ask Mother’s leave.

scenes.reason: Breakfast gives way to a new division of work and a concrete invitation for dinner.

scenes.title: Marmee Takes a Holiday

states.marmee: Marmee gives Jo leave to choose the dinner and declares a holiday from housekeeping.
states.jo: Jo is unsettled by Mother’s morning leisure and heads downstairs at the sound of Beth’s crying.

scenes.reason: Jo consults Mother upstairs before discovering Pip downstairs.

scenes.title: Pip Is Dead

states.jo: Jo confirms that Pip is dead, offers her domino box as a coffin, and promises a funeral.
states.beth: Beth blames her neglect for Pip’s death and begins making him a shroud.
states.amy: Amy suggests warming Pip before accepting the death.

scenes.reason: Jo’s plans are interrupted by the direct consequence of Beth’s neglected daily duty.

scenes.title: Jo Cooks Dinner

states.jo: Jo returns alone to the confused kitchen, stacks the dirty dishes, and discovers that the fire is out.

scenes.reason: Jo leaves the mourning group to assume responsibility for the kitchen and invited meal.

scenes.title: The Overflowing Bread

states.jo: Jo returns from market and bursts in to ask whether overflowing bread has risen enough.
states.meg: Meg tries to silence Jo’s kitchen alarm while entertaining Sallie.
states.sallieGardiner: Sallie laughs at Jo’s floury, disheveled appearance and urgent question.

scenes.reason: After shopping and kitchen work Jo appeals to Meg in front of the visiting Sallie; her work remains anchored in the kitchen.

scenes.title: An Unexpected Dinner Guest

states.meg: Meg receives Miss Crocker politely and tries to answer her searching questions.
states.missCrocker: Miss Crocker arrives without invitation and announces she will stay for dinner.
states.marmee: Marmee checks the household and comforts Beth before going out.
states.beth: Beth works on Pip’s winding sheet while Mother offers a word of comfort.
states.sallieGardiner: Sallie is present during the household call that Jo’s bread emergency interrupted.

scenes.reason: Mother’s departure and Miss Crocker’s arrival change the direct household company.

scenes.title: Jo’s Difficult Menu

states.jo: Jo struggles alone with tough asparagus, burned bread, stubborn dressing, lobster, and lumpy blancmange.

scenes.reason: The narrative returns exclusively to Jo’s final cooking efforts before the dinner bell.

scenes.title: Salted Strawberries

states.jo: Jo serves a tough, smoky dinner and collapses when the salted strawberries expose her final mistake.
states.meg: Meg tries to manage the table and identifies the salt and sour cream.
states.amy: Amy giggles at each failed dish until the disastrous dessert.
states.laurie: Laurie attends Jo’s dinner and makes good-natured efforts to eat it.
states.missCrocker: Miss Crocker tastes the spoiled fruit first, purses her lips, and finally joins the general laughter.

scenes.reason: The invited guests arrive and the private cooking struggle becomes a public meal.

scenes.title: Pip’s Funeral

states.jo: Jo gathers the household for the burial and supplies the epitaph composed while cooking.
states.beth: Beth lays Pip in the fern-shaded grave with tears and covers him with moss.
states.meg: Meg joins the family ceremony and supports Beth.
states.amy: Amy attends the funeral after the disastrous dinner.
states.laurie: Laurie digs Pip’s grave beneath the ferns.

scenes.reason: Dinner ends and the company changes place and purpose for Beth’s sake.

scenes.title: A House Without Its Center

states.jo: Jo spends half the afternoon clearing the failed feast with Meg.
states.meg: Meg works beside Jo and settles for tea and toast after the exhausting cleanup.
states.beth: Beth goes upstairs grieving and finds comfort in putting the unmade beds in order.

scenes.reason: The funeral disperses the cast and leaves the older sisters to face the accumulated household disorder.

scenes.title: Marmee Returns to Work

states.marmee: Marmee comes home and finds the three older girls at work on the neglected household.
states.jo: Jo remains occupied by the cleanup when Mother returns.
states.meg: Meg is still working after the dinner and funeral.
states.beth: Beth continues restoring order after discovering the unmade beds.
states.amy: Amy goes for a drive with Laurie after the sour cream has worsened her temper.
states.laurie: Laurie takes Amy driving while the older sisters put the house right.

scenes.reason: The paragraph explicitly contrasts the drive, upstairs and kitchen chores, and Mother’s homecoming; individual locations prevent a false gathering.

scenes.title: The Sisters Gather on the Porch

states.jo: Jo reaches the porch after more callers, errands, tea, and delayed sewing.
states.meg: Meg sits down exhausted and calls the day uncomfortable.
states.amy: Amy returns to the evening gathering and says the day has not felt like home.
states.beth: Beth looks at the empty cage and misses both Marmee and Pip.

scenes.reason: At twilight the sisters leave the divided duties for one porch gathering; Mother joins afterward.

scenes.title: The Experiment Judged

states.jo: Jo rejects another week of idleness and chooses plain cooking as useful work.
states.meg: Meg recognizes the home’s dependence on shared duty and undertakes Father’s shirts.
states.amy: Amy resolves to learn buttonholes and attend to her speech instead of idling.
states.beth: Beth promises daily lessons and less time spent only on music and dolls.
states.marmee: Marmee returns to her place, reveals the deliberate lesson, and asks each daughter to shoulder her burden again.

scenes.reason: Marmee rejoins the evening circle and turns the difficult day into an explicit household lesson.

chapters.title: CAMP LAURENCE
chapters.notes: Read all 185 paragraphs, including the complete Rig-marole story. Follow Beth’s mail delivery from parlor to study, the sisters’ bedroom preparations, reception on the Laurence lawn, actual boat crossing, all twelve camp participants and bystanders, the smaller private conversations, and return to the lawn. Jo makes coffee; the boys make the fire. Frank, Beth, and sleeping Grace remain present at the story game.

scenes.title: Morning Mail

states.beth: Beth gives Mother the posy and delivers Meg’s letter and single glove.
states.marmee: Marmee receives Laurie’s flowers and watches Meg’s unselfconscious sewing with satisfaction.
states.meg: Meg examines the odd glove and recognizes that Brooke probably translated the German song.

scenes.reason: The post office delivers distinct messages that launch the Camp Laurence outing.

scenes.title: Doctor Jo’s Mail

states.beth: Beth brings Jo the broad hat, book, and two letters in the study.
states.jo: Jo reads Mother’s encouragement, pins it inside her dress, and opens Laurie’s invitation.

scenes.reason: Beth leaves the parlor and delivers Jo’s mail in the study; the two correspondents are absent.

scenes.title: Preparing for Camp Laurence

states.jo: Jo presents Laurie’s invitation and organizes double work so the next day is free.
states.meg: Meg prepares suitable clothes and wonders about the visiting Vaughns.
states.beth: Beth agrees to confront strangers if Jo shields her from boys.
states.amy: Amy displays her mail and plans for the excursion.
states.marmee: Marmee permits the outing and supports each daughter’s preparations.

scenes.reason: Laurie’s invitation becomes a household plan with explicit work and social goals.

scenes.title: The Two Houses Stir

states.jo: Jo wakes and laughs at Amy’s nose ornament while preparing for the camp outing.
states.meg: Meg has put an extra row of curl papers across her forehead.
states.beth: Beth has taken her doll Joanna to bed before the day’s separation.
states.amy: Amy sleeps with a drawing-board clothespin on her nose to improve its shape.

scenes.reason: The next morning both households prepare and the full party begins to assemble.

scenes.title: Beth’s Window Reports

states.beth: Beth reports the preparations and arrivals visible through the bedroom window.
states.jo: Jo defends her broad hat and leads her sisters toward the gathering.
states.meg: Meg recognizes Ned and Sallie and checks whether her outfit is right.
states.amy: Amy finishes preparing with her sisters before they set out.

chapters.title: FRIEND

scenes.title: The Castle in Spain

scenes.reason: The chapter opens by reconnecting Jo’s daily work with her literary ambition.

scenes.reason: Jo turns renewed ambition into a different market and enters its office.

states.mrDashwood: Mr. Dashwood offers payment, demands omitted sermons, and teaches Jo what his readers buy.

scenes.reason: The editor’s decision brings Jo back for terms and revision.

scenes.title: Three Months of Sensation
scenes.reason: The first sale becomes a sustained period of formulaic paid writing.

scenes.title: Jo Learns to Read Character
scenes.reason: Moral unease changes the focus from plots to Jo’s observation of Bhaer.

scenes.title: Writing Without Knowledge

scenes.reason: The bonfire ends one practice but begins a period of unsuccessful corrective experiments.

scenes.title: A True Friend

states.jo: Jo continues teaching and living quietly while her friendship with Bhaer lays foundations deeper than publication.
states.professorBhaer: Bhaer supports Jo through ordinary kindness and intellectual companionship.

scenes.reason: Jo’s pen rests while the chapter assesses the outwardly uneventful winter.
